remaining_cautions.evidence_context: CAMP/dbAMP entry-level labels indicate antibacterial/antifungal or broad mammalian-cell activity, but the primary paper reports no significant direct antimicrobial activity for HAP-1 up to 80 uM and presents HAP-1 as an inhibitor of ApHt_20 activity.

Primary text supports no detectable hemolytic activity at 80 uM but does not specify human erythrocyte target or method details; DBAASP human-erythrocyte rows remain source_conflict rather than clean source_verified.
Figure 3A supports the qualitative disk-diffusion inhibition-zone loss at 140 nM HAP-1 with 40 nM ApHt_20, but local text does not provide an exact zone diameter.
The paper proposes HAP-1/ApHt_20 interaction after excluding pH change, but local material lacks a direct binding, membrane, or structural interaction assay.
